problem: Polygon-based referring-expression segmentation methods penalize vertex sets that describe the same polygon in a different order, and RES models handle neither multi-sentence manipulation instructions nor objects outside the camera's field of view.
motivation: Domestic service robots need accurate masks (not boxes) of the target object from open-vocabulary, multi-sentence instructions such as those in REVERIE. Existing RES models (LAVT, SeqTR, MDSM) struggle on this harder setting, and order-sensitive vertex losses make training inefficient.
key_idea: Train a polygon-vertex predictor with an optimal-transport (Sinkhorn) matching loss that is invariant to vertex order, and add LLM-paraphrased instructions, GPT-4V image descriptions, OpenScene 3D open-vocabulary features and SAM-segment attention as inputs.
insight: Every module helps mIoU in the ablation: removing SBAE/SAM costs 6.39 points, removing PML 5.09 points, removing VCI 2.89 points. Removing OVA lowers mIoU by only 0.8 but raises P@0.7 by 4.95 points, since 3D context features can pull attention toward surrounding nouns such as a sink instead of the target picture. Error analysis shows the main bottlenecks are language-vision grounding errors (43) and reference/spatial resolution errors (32).
method: LLM Paraphraser: GPT-3.5-turbo merges the multi-sentence instruction into one sentence about the target object, embedded with text-embedding-ada-002 (h_llp).
Visual Context Interpreter (VCI): gpt-4-vision-preview describes the image (attributes, spatial relations, common sense), embedded with ada-002 (h_vci).

Open-Vocabulary 3D Aggregator (OVA): takes the N_near=10 point-cloud points closest to the camera position, extracts pretrained OpenScene (CLIP-aligned) features, then upsamples and max-pools them (h_ova) to cover out-of-view objects.

Segment-Based Attentional Enhancer (SBAE): SAM produces a segmentation image; multi-resolution DarkNet-53 features from the image and the SAM image are concatenated and cross-attended with concatenated [h_llp, h_vci, h_ova].
Optimal Transport Vertex Predictor (OTVP): a transformer encoder-decoder (3 layers each) predicts polygon vertices.

Polygon Matching Loss (PML): optimal-transport loss between predicted and GT vertex sets, with L2 cost, entropy regularization and the Sinkhorn algorithm. Training uses L1 loss up to epoch 79 and PML for epochs 80-90.

setting.backbone: Trained transformer (SBAE cross-attention + OTVP encoder-decoder, 320M params) on top of frozen GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4V, ada-002, SAM, OpenScene/CLIP and DarkNet-53
setting.training_data: SHIMRIE-3D (built by the authors from REVERIE and Matterport3D): 10,153 training samples from seen environments
setting.observation: monocular RGB image (640x480) + Matterport3D 3D point cloud + language instruction
setting.action_space: not applicable (predicts polygon-vertex segmentation mask, not navigation actions)
setting.simulator: none (Matterport3D static images and point clouds)
setting.privileged: Matterport3D point clouds with known camera position; annotation-derived masks used for training only

numbers.extra: mean of 5 runs; test set of 362 samples from unseen environments
numbers.evidence: Table I: Comparison with baseline methods on the SHIMRIE-3D dataset

numbers_note: Not a navigation benchmark; results are on the authors' own SHIMRIE-3D dataset. Standard deviations were omitted.
results: The full model reaches 38.16 mIoU, 48.85 P@0.5 and 22.29 P@0.7, beating the best baseline LAVT (28.16 / 26.46 / 18.75) by 10.00 mIoU and 22.39 P@0.5. It also beats SeqTR (21.84 mIoU) and MDSM (24.36 mIoU). The abstract's +16.32% claim compares against the polygon-based SeqTR.
limitations: Failures come mainly from grounding and reference-resolution errors, from VCI (GPT-4V) hallucinations, and from ambiguous instructions.
OVA can distract attention toward context objects, and the dataset is small (362 test samples) with single-target images only.
Depends on expensive closed LLM APIs (GPT-4V, GPT-3.5) and Matterport3D point clouds with known camera positions.
